context.description: A stalled builder stream is cancelled and prompted again in the same attempt

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review at HEAD 5fb09be29c (after D8/D9 fixes in supervise/run.ts and harness.ts); test unchanged since 6841bc0e5d; trial bun test 1 pass 0 fail. Given a building task whose stream goes quiet with no tool running: the real RunSupervisor (root actor, SimulatedClock) over the T1.1 subtree resumed with T1.1 building spawns the real TaskSupervisor; asserts T1.1 building with attempts 1, the first prompt is the attempt message (role=builder line) in ses_T1.1 claimed with watch true; no turn.tool event is ever sent; a real part delta on the event bus at 1.5 s restarts the timer (3 s in: only run.resumed stored, no cancel), which proves the idle clock is driven by stream activity. When the stream idle time passes: 0.5 s more of quiet passes the scripted 2 s streamIdle. Then the turn is cancelled and task.stalled is recorded: cancels == [ses_T1.1] (the real builderTurn worker's interruption) and the last stored fact is task.stalled T1.1 'stall: no stream activity for 2 s'. And the builder is prompted again with the continue message in the same attempt: the second prompt equals exactly {ses_T1.1, task-builder, the literal D7 continue message}, sent by the real run supervisor's unit.moved dispatch; same session. And no nudge and no attempt is spent: T1.1 stays building with attempts 1, stored types are exactly [run.resumed, task.stalled] (no task.nudged), the task supervisor's nudges context is 0; a second quiet period repeats it (two cancels, a third continue prompt, still attempt 1, nudges 0, each turn claimed the same session). Only the session side (prompts that never end) is scripted. Every step is asserted specifically on the real code.
